guidance: The mansion overlooks the hub. The haunted house stands on a rise at the west edge of the sac; its flagpole faces the circle every line crosses (inferred from LP3 0:27:53's view).
The NPC points at the door. The Thin Man stands on the path to the boarded house; the goal card shows him by the gate (LP3 0:23:21–0:23:22). The axe is an item the HUD tracks (G3 p074).
Letters and lines lead to the front wall. G1's T is on the wall in front of the house; G3's E above its side banked wall; G3's long scoring line ends at the house; the fifth pumpkin is on its porch.
Inside, glass marks the way. The upstairs window is the target of the backyard ramp; the front glass frames the pole ("On the other side of the glass ahead", PS34).
Hidden on purpose: the hallway "seems to lead to a dead end" (G3 p074); the backyard and the upstairs are out of sight until the wall transfer.
designLogic: Locked-house tape. The tape hangs on the front of the building that overlooks the hub, but can only be reached from inside, after an errand. It is the first THPS3 tape behind a fetch quest.
The errand tours the level. The axe is at the construction site (south), the Thin Man by the trailer park path (west): the errand crosses the sac and introduces two areas.
An inside-out loop. In at the front door, through the hallway, out to the back, up the back wall, in at the top, out through the front window: one building, walked through completely.
Speed, then precision. The backyard gives speed for the tall ramp; the hallway asks to "slow down and align" before the last jump to the pole (G3 p073).
Glass as doors. Two breakable windows bracket the upstairs; each is a commitment point.
A soft finish at the start. The pole is over the front yard by the start tree; a miss or the exit (Spooky Drop) returns the player to the hub.
Lines rehearse the route. G3's long scoring line ends with the wall transfer into the backyard (step 3) and Look Out Behind You! (the backyard wall launch).
The revert links the backyard. LP3 keeps the combo through the yard with a revert after a 540 cannonball; the tape's speed-building step is THPS3's new vert-to-manual link in action.
A secret area that is a park. The backyard has its own gaps (six), a stat point and the launch to the roof wires; the tape route uses its geometry rather than adding a special path.
Progression across THPS3's first three tapes. Foundry: no unlock, open upper layer. Canada: a switch on the route. Suburbia: a fetch quest across the level and a building interior.
The PS1 edition had no interior. Its tape floats over the sac by a boom; the PS2 build moved the challenge into a gated building with an NPC.
The remake keeps the route and fills the house. Cash, a plushie and a stat point in the backyard, and a periodic door into "the Abyss" (pro goal).
remakeChanges: Tape: same route (PS34; LP34 10 s from the hallway); pcgamesn calls the pole a 'tree branch'
Goals: Heelflip the Trailer Hop alternative dropped; High Combo 15,000; five pro goals (COMBO, Manual Around the Sac, Pizza Guy in the Abyss, Impress the Skaters)
Three letter sets -> one set (≈ G1)
COMBO letters on the gray-house line (pro goal)
Haunted front door opens periodically into 'the Abyss' (pro goal)
New pickups: Cash ×4 (one on a moving plane), Hidden Deck, Iron Galaxy logo, plushie, 3 stat points (backyard and wires populated)
PS1 edition (2001): different layout and goals; tape over the cul-de-sac by a boom, no interior
transfer: Locked-house crystal. A two-storey house on a rise at the hub's edge, with a short pole (grindable, ≈ 3 m long) projecting from the upper floor over the front yard; the crystal on the pole, ≥ 7 m above the yard below.
Errand gate. The door is boarded; an NPC opens it when the player brings an item found on a rail at the far side of the level (pickup shown on the HUD).

Inside-out route. Hallway → a wall to vert-transfer over (quarter pipe + vert-air) → a bowl-like backyard → a tall launch ramp into a smashable upper window → a short hallway → smashable front window → pole grind (snap radius 2.1 m makes the short pole fair).
Speed then calm. Put a speed pad or bowl wall before the launch ramp; make the upstairs hallway short and straight so players line up before the window.
Soft exit. The fall from the pole lands in the front yard next to the spawn.
Keep walkers off. The porch roof below the pole must be unstandable or ≥ 3 m below it with no grab edge; the pole ≥ 6.5 m above any standable surface outside the house.
openQuestions: The TAS's tape pickup is not visible: the goal registers in the end-of-run messages (3:25) after the fifth pumpkin on the haunted porch (3:20–3:21), where the skater "kisses the rail" twice beside the front door; a direct touch of the pole from the porch is possible but unconfirmed.
Heights of the front yard, the upper floor and the pole are estimates.
G3's tape text names a "Haunted Backyard Transfer" gap that is not in its gap list.
The PS1 edition's tape route (map only; a boom reaches towards it).
PCGamesN's "tree branch" vs the flagpole in every other source (remake).
Whether the remake's interior layout differs in detail (only 10 s of LP34 seen).
